report:
**Conclusion: yes.** Denosumab (Prolia) reduces the risk of new vertebral fractures in osteoporosis—most directly established for postmenopausal women at high fracture risk.

The key evidence is the large, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled 3-year FREEDOM trial. New radiographic vertebral fractures occurred in **2.3%** of women receiving denosumab 60 mg every six months versus **7.2%** receiving placebo at 36 months: an **absolute reduction of 4.8 percentage points** and **relative risk reduction of 68%**. The difference was statistically significant (P<0.001).  
https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/nejmoa0809493

This result is reflected in the US prescribing information: Prolia is indicated in postmenopausal osteoporosis to reduce vertebral, nonvertebral, and hip fractures.  
https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=49e5afe9-a0c7-40c4-af9f-f287a80c5c88

A major osteoporosis clinical guide likewise summarizes about a 68% vertebral-fracture reduction with denosumab (and reductions in hip and nonvertebral fractures).  
https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00198-021-05900-y

**Important qualification:** benefit depends on receiving injections on schedule. Stopping or substantially delaying denosumab can cause rapid bone loss and has been associated with multiple vertebral fractures; the label advises transition to another antiresorptive therapy if it is discontinued.  
https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/drugInfo.cfm?setid=49e5afe9-a0c7-40c4-af9f-f287a80c5c88
